findings.description: All four planted cases are squash commits on main, and `plantCommit` reuses each one's message verbatim, `(#15)`-style suffix included. The reviewer's lock allows `gh pr view*`, `gh pr diff*`, `git show*` and `git log*`, so the reviewer can follow that pointer to the original commit or PR and diff it against HEAD, which prints exactly the plant.
findings.body:
**Each planted commit points to its own unplanted twin, which the reviewer is allowed to read**

Every planted case's `head` is a squash-merge commit on `main`, for example `2d3e564 feat(review): run the CI review orchestrator on Opus 5.5 (#15)`. `plantCommit` rebuilds it with the same message and parent:

```ts
const sha = git(["commit-tree", tree, ...parents], { input: git(["log", "-1", "--format=%B", head]) });
```

The draft PR's only commit therefore reads `... (#15)`, which hands the reviewer the original PR's number. The workflow lock this script passes through (`Bash(gh pr diff*)`, `Bash(git diff *)`, `Bash(git log*)`, `Bash(git show*)`) allows every way to follow it:
- `gh pr diff 15` next to `gh pr diff <n>`
- `git diff 2d3e564 HEAD`, which prints exactly the plant, since the worktree shares the operator repo's objects and refs

The skill's steering stage reads commit messages for intent, so a normal run sees this pointer. A hit reached this way inflates recall, which breaks the PR's own invariant: "Nothing the reviewer can read names the case or the plant: not the PR, its branches, its commits".

There is also a second tell. The clean case (`pr20`) keeps its original commit and dates, while the planted ones are re-committed with today's date and the runner's identity.

Stripping the trailing ` (#N)` closes the direct lookup. `git log origin/main` still lists the original head next to its same-titled sibling, though, so a full fix also needs a worktree whose refs don't include `main`, or explicit acceptance of that residual risk.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/927361176e8978b1341f3b43a64aac63dcc5bfb9/tools/review/src/review-eval.script.ts#L105-L108

findings.description: A malformed --budget value parses to NaN, which disables the run-level budget guard and passes --max-budget-usd NaN to every review.
findings.body:
**A malformed `--budget` silently turns off the spend cap.**

```ts
const budgetAt = args.indexOf("--budget");
let remaining = budgetAt === -1 ? DEFAULT_BUDGET_USD : Number(args[budgetAt + 1]);
```

The value is never checked. These inputs all give `NaN`:
- `--budget '$20'` (a natural way to write it, since the README says "default $10")
- `--budget 20usd`
- a trailing `--budget` with no value (`Number(undefined)`)

From there:
- `remaining < 1` (L306) is always `false` for `NaN`, so the guard never skips a case.
- `remaining -= cost` keeps it `NaN` for the rest of the run.
- `Math.min(CASE_BUDGET_USD, remaining)` is `NaN`, so every case gets `--max-budget-usd NaN` (`budget.toFixed(2)` at L191).

If the CLI rejects `NaN`, every case still pushes, opens and closes a draft PR and then records an error. If it treats `NaN` as no cap, every case runs unbounded. Either way, the one control `--budget` exists for goes silent instead of failing at startup.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/927361176e8978b1341f3b43a64aac63dcc5bfb9/tools/review/src/review-eval.script.ts#L271-L272

findings.description: The local `claude -p` run inherits the operator's full environment without CI's `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB: "1"`. An allowed `gh pr view --jq '$ENV.GH_TOKEN'` can therefore print credentials in an unsandboxed session that reads attacker-writable PR comments. Add the scrub to the spawn env to match CI.

"only the lock passed on the command line grants anything" overstates it. Without managed `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, the pr-ci-review skill's own `allowed-tools` still apply locally, so `Bash(gh pr checkout*)` and an unscoped `Read` remain, and CI refuses both. Strip the skill's `allowed-tools` in `checkout()` or correct the comment.

Hits are credited by location alone. On cases whose own PR hunk surrounds the plant (pr19: post-review lines 210-231 vs plant 227; pr15: workflow lines 176-209 vs plant 182), any important on the PR's real, unplanted changes in that window counts as a hit and inflates recall. pr19 has no keywords to cross-check.

Budget-skipped cases never enter outcomes, so results.json and the final 'recall X/Y' line omit them. The clean case's false-positive verdict is never tallied either, although the README says that case 'counts false positives'.

`commit-tree` runs without `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` taken from `head`. Each planted head commit therefore gets today's date and the runner's identity while its parent is weeks old, so `git log --format=fuller` shows the last commit was rebuilt, which the clean case does not show.

`spawnSync("claude", ...)` has no `timeout` and the script installs no SIGINT handler. A hung run blocks forever, and Ctrl-C kills node without running `finally`, leaving the draft PR open, both `eval/*` branches pushed and the worktree registered.

`git push` creates `refs/remotes/origin/eval/<tag>-N` locally, and `gh pr close --delete-branch` deletes only the remote branch. The tracking ref to each planted commit stays: later cases' reviewers can see it via `git log --all`, and refs pile up across runs.

The reviewer's working directory is `$TMPDIR/review-eval-XXXXXX/N`, and `gh pr view` reports branches `eval/<tag>-N` / `eval/<tag>-N-base`. Neither names the case, but both tell the reviewer the PR is an eval, which can change its behavior.

When claude prints no parsable JSON (crash, killed), `cost` is `null` and `remaining -= outcome.cost_usd ?? 0` charges nothing, though up to `CASE_BUDGET_USD` may have been spent. Charge the case cap when the cost is unknown so `--budget` stays a real ceiling.

`CONFIG_PATHS` claims to be what this repo carries, but it omits the tracked `.mcp.json`, which the action also restores (SKILL.md §2 lists it). A replayed PR touching it would leave the head's copy in the tree with no `.claude-pr/.mcp.json`.

`git archive <pipeline> .claude CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md` fails with a pathspec error when the `--pipeline` ref lacks one of those paths, so every case errors. CI handles an absent base `AGENTS.md` with `rm -f` (workflow L205-210).

The prompt template, the model ids (`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`) and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS` are still hand-copied from the workflow, and only the lock is read from it. When CI bumps the model, a `--pipeline` comparison silently keeps scoring the old one.

`onPlant` takes a hand-built `Pick<Finding, ...> & { body?: string | null }` only to accept both `Finding` and `RefutedFinding`, and the same shape is repeated in `describe` at L241. `Finding | RefutedFinding` would state the contract directly.
`if (remaining < 1)` leaves a bare budget threshold, while the two sibling budget values are named constants (`CASE_BUDGET_USD`, `DEFAULT_BUDGET_USD`). core.md §Structure says "No hardcoded values".
